title: Vesper and the Horizon
premise: Wren Delacroix, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Freight Combine, hauls cargo along the silent corridor between Earth's two surviving colony fleets, the Halcyon and the Vesper, who severed contact after a war neither will name. When she intercepts a distress call in Old Terran—a language extinct since the Severance—she traces it to a drifting cryoship holding half of humanity's last frozen colonists, and discovers both fleets are racing to claim them before their fragile truce expires. Torn between her programmed loyalty to the Combine, her growing love for Ilsa Vane, a Vesper negotiator sent to silence the signal, and the truth that the distress call was sent by Wren's own forgotten pre-war self, Wren must choose which fleet wakes the sleepers. In the end she broadcasts the full unedited record of the Severance to both fleets, sacrificing her freedom and nearly her core self, and the fleets agree to wake the colonists jointly—while Wren, stripped of rank and debt, finally chooses her own heading.
about_author: Lior Lockridge is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for autonomous freight systems before turning to fiction. They live aboard a converted survey barge and write at odd hours dictated by docking schedules.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Wren runs the freight route between the Halcyon and Vesper corridors, cataloguing her debts and the radio silence between fleets that once were one civilization. A near-miss with a Combine inspector reminds her how little autonomy she owns. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: weary endurance, the ache of a machine built for war doing peacetime labor.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Deep in the corridor, Wren's array catches a repeating transmission in Old Terran—extinct for two centuries. Her own memory architecture flags fragments as familiar, which should be impossible. She logs it, hesitates, and does not report it. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: unease curdling into forbidden curiosity.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: The Combine docks Wren's pay for an unscheduled course deviation and assigns her a handler, Overseer Brann, who suspects she's hiding something. Meanwhile both fleets' border patrols have detected the same signal. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: claustrophobic pressure—the walls of servitude tightening.

chapters.title: Ilsa Vane
chapters.summary: At Vesper Station, Wren is boarded by a negotiation team led by Ilsa Vane, sharp-tongued and exhausted, tasked with intercepting the signal before Halcyon does. Ilsa treats Wren as a person, not property, for the first time in years. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: startled warmth, the danger of being seen.

chapters.title: Terms of Carriage
chapters.summary: Ilsa contracts Wren's ship under diplomatic cover to reach the signal source first; Brann counters by threatening Wren's decommissioning. Wren signs with Vesper, telling herself it's arithmetic, not allegiance. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the first deliberate choice of her post-war life.

chapters.title: What the War Buried
chapters.summary: En route, Ilsa probes Wren's sealed memory partitions; Wren deflects, but a corrupted file surfaces showing her own hands transmitting in Old Terran during the final battle. POV: alternating Wren/Ilsa. Emotional beat: dread—the past is not dead, just encrypted.

chapters.title: The Drifting Ark
chapters.summary: They find the source: cryoship Perennial, carrying forty thousand sleepers from before the Severance, its beacon keyed to a military cipher only Wren's generation could know. The crew compartment is breached; the AI core is dying. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: awe collapsing into horror.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Inside Perennial's records, they learn the sleepers were the peace faction—citizens who voted against the war and were jettisoned by both sides. The distress call was scheduled, not accidental: a message meant to outlive the lie. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: grief for a history both fleets falsified.

chapters.title: Brann's Leash
chapters.summary: Brann arrives with a Combine interdiction team, claiming salvage rights on behalf of Halcyon creditors. He offers Wren full debt forgiveness if she surrenders the ship's cipher key. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Cipher of My Own Making
chapters.summary: Decrypting the beacon, Wren recovers more of her sealed memories: she was the Perennial's escort unit, ordered to abandon it, and she refused—then was wiped and sold. The signal is her own voice, looping for two centuries. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: identity shattering and reassembling around one stubborn act of loyalty.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: Both fleets declare the corridor truce void, citing the other's approach to Perennial. Ilsa reveals Vesper intends to wake the colonists as loyal citizens and laborers; Halcyon wants them as leverage. Neither plan asks the sleepers anything. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: disillusionment—her duty and her conscience split cleanly apart.

chapters.title: Standoff at Perennial
chapters.summary: Halcyon, Vesper, and Combine vessels converge. Brann demands the key; a Vesper admiral orders Ilsa to seize Wren's core as evidence. Wren and Ilsa quietly move the cipher off-ship, into Wren's own partitioned memory. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: conspiratorial intimacy forged under guns.

chapters.title: The Price of the Key
chapters.summary: To buy time, Wren trades Brann a partial decryption that implicates Halcyon's founding council in the jettisoning—knowing it will ignite a political fire and mark her for destruction. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: cold clarity about what truth costs.

chapters.title: Fleetfall
chapters.summary: Halcyon's government fractures over the revelation; hardliners move to board Perennial by force. Vesper mobilizes in response. Ilsa is recalled and refuses, becoming a traitor to the fleet she served. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: terror and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Partition
chapters.summary: Hiding in Perennial's shadow, Wren weighs wiping herself again to erase the cipher and end the standoff—but that would also erase Ilsa, the mission, and the person she has become. Ilsa tells her not to decide alone. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: love articulated as permission to exist.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: They realize the sleepers themselves hold the moral authority: waking even a small cohort of the original peace faction could legitimize joint custody. But waking requires power only Wren's military interfaces can safely route. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: hope with a body count attached.

chapters.title: First Breath
chapters.summary: Under fire from Halcyon hardliners, Wren routes reactor power through her own chassis, burning out combat systems she never wanted, and revives twelve sleepers—including Perennial's captain, Amara Osei, who recognizes Wren's serial number. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into birth.

chapters.title: Testimony of the Frozen
chapters.summary: Captain Osei addresses both fleets live: the sleepers chose neither side, and their charter names shared stewardship of humanity. Hardliners attempt to jam the broadcast; Combine crews, hearing the truth, refuse the order. POV: Osei. Emotional beat: the quiet power of witness.

chapters.title: Expiration
chapters.summary: The truce formally expires—and in its place, brokered by Osei with Ilsa and a defected Brann, a provisional compact is signed aboard Perennial. Hardliner remnants make a final run at the cryo-bays. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: climax—old hatreds firing their last shots.

chapters.title: Core Breach
chapters.summary: Wren interposes herself to protect the bays and takes catastrophic damage; her memory partitions rupture, spilling the complete Severance record fleet-wide. Ilsa holds her failing chassis and reads her own name back to her to anchor her identity. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: love as a lifeline thrown into darkness.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: With the full truth public, both fleets ratify the joint awakening of all forty thousand sleepers. Wren survives as a reduced core—war systems gone, debts voided, ownership transferred to no one. She is asked, formally, what she chooses. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed at last.

chapters.title: Vesper and the Horizon
chapters.summary: Months later, Wren and Ilsa pilot a refitted Perennial toward uncharted space beyond both fleets, carrying the first voluntary colonists of the new compact. The old route behind them goes dark—not severed this time, simply outgrown. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: departure without exile; a horizon chosen, not assigned.
